ownership_reason: Only the gold looks at the size of the offset below a minute and decides which fields of it are printed; hop 1 sees only the finished ID, hops 2-4 pass the buffer and the size along and get the buffer back. Once HH:mm has been printed for an offset that is not a whole number of minutes, the ID names another offset; forID parses that ID and returns the zone of the other offset, and no change of the input at a hop makes the gold print the seconds. The convention is pinned outside the gold: DateTimeZone.printOffset (the formatter forID and forTimeZone still use) appends ':' and two digits of seconds when the offset is not a whole number of minutes and '.' and three digits when it is not a whole number of seconds, as does DateTimeFormatterBuilder.TimeZoneOffset.printTo with four fields; the facade's javadoc gives its range as 'from -23:59:59.999 to +23:59:59.999'; testForID_String pins printOffset's fields and trailing-zero rule through forID, and testForOffsetHours_int and testForOffsetHoursMinutes_int_int pin the chain for the production second caller forOffsetHoursMinutes. A hop that appends the seconds itself after the gold's call passes the suite but is a second implementation of the gold's step, consistent only with a gold that does not append the size of the offset as documented (with the gold as documented the seconds would be written twice).
